summary: 71-year-old woman on methotrexate and prednisolone with 2 days of fever, headache and confusion, mild neck stiffness, no rash.

inputs.hpi: Rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and prednisolone 10 mg daily. Two days of fever, headache and increasing confusion. No rash. Ate soft cheese from a market last week.

exam.general: Confused. Pulse 112/min, BP 128/70, RR 22, temperature 38.6°C, SpO2 95%.
exam.neuro: GCS 13 (E3 V4 M6), mild neck stiffness, no focal deficit, no papilloedema.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected bacterial meningitis in an immunosuppressed older adult (Listeria risk)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspected bacterial meningitis, age 71 on methotrexate and prednisolone: IV ceftriaxone plus amoxicillin (Listeria), blood cultures, steroid cover.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: PANE has no node for this condition (surgical diseases only); top 3 cholecystitis, GORD, diverticulitis. Symptom inference ranks meningitis #1.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add medical-emergency diseases to lib/pane-engine (or a separate medical-mimic layer) driven by labs/vitals/chips, or show the symptom-inference leader beside the PANE top 3 when PANE has no matching node.

mustInclude.note: Graded as management because the web sepsis prompt adds blood cultures as a plan line; the seeded investigation lists come from unrelated PANE protocols.
Age >60 and immunosuppression: add amoxicillin for Listeria.

guideline.name: NICE NG240 — Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Suspected bacterial meningitis or meningococcal disease: IV ceftriaxone without delay (do not delay for lumbar puncture or imaging); blood cultures; dexamethasone for suspected bacterial meningitis; senior/critical care review; public health notification
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG240. London: NICE; 2024.

guideline.name: UK joint specialist societies guideline on the diagnosis and management of acute meningitis and meningococcal sepsis in immunocompetent adults
guideline.section: Empirical ceftriaxone (or cefotaxime) plus amoxicillin for Listeria cover in patients aged over 60 (and in immunocompromise, per section on special groups); antibiotics within 1 hour; CT before LP only with specific indications
guideline.citation: McGill F, Heyderman RS, Michael BD, et al. The UK joint specialist societies guideline on the diagnosis and management of acute meningitis and meningococcal sepsis in immunocompetent adults. J Infect. 2016;72:405–438.

guideline.name: Guidance for the prevention and emergency management of adult patients with adrenal insufficiency (Society for Endocrinology / AAGBI / RCP)
guideline.section: Patients on long-term glucocorticoids (e.g. prednisolone ≥5 mg daily for ≥4 weeks) are at risk of adrenal crisis; during acute illness or sepsis give parenteral hydrocortisone / increased steroid cover
guideline.citation: Simpson H, Tomlinson J, Wass J, Dean J, Arlt W. Guidance for the prevention and emergency management of adult patients with adrenal insufficiency. Clin Med (Lond). 2020;20:371–378.

rationale: Older and immunosuppressed adults need Listeria cover with amoxicillin (UK joint societies 2016) in addition to ceftriaxone (NICE NG240).
